Agencies may request from OMB an extension of up to one year for a particular use of AI that cannot feasibly meet the minimum requirements by the specified date. Extension requests must be submitted prior to October 15, 2024, and must be accompanied by a detailed justification explaining why the agency cannot achieve compliance for the use of AI in question and what practices the agency has in place to mitigate the risks from noncompliance.

Regarding waivers, an agency Chief AI Officer (CAIO) may waive one or more of the requirements for a specific covered AI application or component after making a written determination based on a system-specific and context-specific risk assessment. This assessment must conclude that fulfilling the requirement would increase risks to safety or rights overall or create an unacceptable impediment to critical agency operations. CAIOs must centrally track waivers, reassess them if there are significant changes to the conditions or context in which the AI is used, and report to OMB within 30 days of granting or revoking any waiver, detailing the scope, justification, and supporting evidence.
